purpose: How every backend failure becomes something a customer can act on. One table, shared by every tool, so a code the catalog does not enumerate still lands somewhere sensible. Prose reference: ../ARCHITECTURE.md section 9.
reading_order: 1. A tool's own `errors[]` entry in catalog.json wins — it is the specific handling.
2. Otherwise this file's `codes` table, keyed on error.code.
3. Otherwise this file's `categories` table, keyed on error.category, which is present on EVERY error from all three backend services.
4. Never branch on error.message. It is human copy and it changes.

explain.means: Tell the customer what happened in their own language and stop. There is nothing to retry.
explain.copy_rule: Say what is true and what they can do next. Never quote the error code or the English message.

reprompt.means: The customer supplied something the platform would not take. Ask again for that one value.
reprompt.copy_rule: Name the field and the constraint. `details.fields[]` is populated on VALIDATION_ERROR and each entry maps to one thing to ask about.

disambiguate.means: More than one thing matched. Offer the candidates and let the customer choose.
disambiguate.copy_rule: Never pick for them, and never pick the first.

retry_with_backoff.means: A third party or a limiter refused. Wait and try again, bounded.
retry_with_backoff.policy: 3 attempts, 2s / 8s / 30s. Respect Retry-After and details.retryAfterSeconds when present. Then fall through to escalate_to_support.
retry_with_backoff.copy_rule: Tell them it is being retried. Do not say 'error'; this is not their fault and not fixable by them.

handoff_to_web.means: This cannot be done in a chat window. Send a link and say what to do there.
handoff_to_web.copy_rule: Say why, in one clause. 'Cards are paid on the website' is better than an unexplained link.

require_login.means: The sender is not resolvable, or holds no customer role. Offer the sign-in or registration path.
require_login.copy_rule: For a Telegram chat with no contact shared, the answer is the contact prompt, not a link.

abandon_flow.means: Something the flow was carrying is stale or wrong. Drop the flow state and start the step again from a clean read.
abandon_flow.copy_rule: Apologise once, briefly, and re-ask. Never re-send arguments the flow was holding.

escalate_to_support.means: The platform cannot resolve this by itself. Offer to open a ticket, pre-filled.
escalate_to_support.copy_rule: Always quote the requestId. On an internal or external_service failure it is the only handle anybody has.

silent_ignore.means: The failure does not concern the customer. Log it and say nothing.
silent_ignore.copy_rule: Only for bookkeeping calls the customer never asked for, such as recording that a product card was shown.

authentication.note: Never retry. On the bot surface this almost always means the messaging identity could not be resolved, not that a token expired.

authorization.note: Signed in, but this is not theirs. Do not retry and do not hint that the thing exists.

validation.note: details.fields[] maps to what to ask about.

not_found.note: Treat as absent. NEVER infer existence from a 404 — the platform answers 404 for 'not yours' on purpose, so 'that is not your order' and 'no such order' are the same answer and must be phrased as one.

conflict.note: The state moved underneath the flow. Re-read, then let the customer decide again — never resend the same intent.

business_rule.note: Well-formed and refused on purpose. error.message explains which rule and is written to be shown. This is not a fault and must not be apologised for as one.

rate_limit.note: Respect Retry-After. Prefer the RateLimit: remaining= header to slow down before being refused.

external_service.note: message is a fixed generic sentence and details is omitted, in every environment. requestId is the only handle.

internal.note: Same opacity as external_service. Show the requestId.

RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.note: Customers are bounded at 600/min per user and 1200/min per address. A chat bot reaching either is looping.

WEBHOOK_SECRET_INVALID.note: Configuration, not a customer problem. It breaks /connect and sign-in together, so an outage here looks like several unrelated faults at once. Alert rather than retry.

AUTH_ROLE_NOT_FOUND.note: On the bot surface: the sender is a vendor, agency or agent. They keep /help, /connect and /reset-password and reach nothing customer-scoped. A customer role is never auto-provisioned.

BOT_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED.note: No account for this messaging identity. Offer registration.

BOT_IDENTITY_NEEDS_CONTACT.note: Telegram, first contact. The answer is the request_contact keyboard.

MAGIC_CONTACT_UNVERIFIED.note: Relay error.message verbatim. It is written for a chat window and does not read as an accusation, because the ordinary way to hit it is tapping the wrong contact.

MAGIC_CODE_INVALID.note: Deliberately one code for four situations. NEVER write copy that says 'no account with that number' — differentiating it would make the endpoint a registration oracle.

CATALOG_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND.note: Absent, draft, archived, suspended, or its vendor is suspended — indistinguishable on purpose, so never speculate about which.

CATALOG_INSUFFICIENT_STOCK.note: `available` is what the shopper can actually buy, after other in-flight checkouts. Offer the available quantity as a next step.

CART_MIXED_PRODUCT_TYPES.note: One basket holds physical OR digital, never both. Offer to check out what is there first — never clear it without asking.

CART_SERVICE_PRODUCT_NOT_ALLOWED.note: Services are booked against a calendar, not carted.

CART_ITEM_NOT_FOUND.note: A stale reference — re-read the cart before answering.

CART_VARIANT_PRODUCT_MISMATCH.note: The flow built a bad pair. Re-read the product; never retry with the same ids.

ORDER_DELIVERY_ADDRESS_REQUIRED.note: reason `selected_address_not_geocoded` means an address the customer explicitly chose is unusable because it was typed rather than picked from address search. Take them into the address flow; do not just say 'invalid address'.

ORDER_NO_DELIVERY_AGENCY.note: A platform-side gap, not the customer's doing.

ORDER_CANCEL_REQUIRES_REFUND.note: The order is paid. This endpoint refunds nothing; open a ticket.

CANCELLATION_NOT_ALLOWED.note: The SELLER's policy, not the platform's. Quote their terms.

ORDER_NOT_FOUND.note: Also returned when the order is somebody else's. Phrase as one answer.

COD_ORDER_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_LIMIT.note: Quote the cap. It is actionable: a smaller basket, or online payment.

COD_COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND.note: Not a cash order, not picked up yet, or already collected. Say which is likely from the shipment status rather than guessing.

SHIPMENT_CONFIRMATION_NOT_ALLOWED.note: When paymentMethod is cash_on_delivery the answer is the delivery code, not a confirmation. Offer that instead.

PAYMENT_OPERATOR_UNDETERMINED.note: Ask MTN or Orange. Guessing reaches the customer as 'payment declined'.

PAYMENT_INITIATION_FAILED.note: A 502 is transport-level. A gateway REFUSAL is not this — it is HTTP 200 with status FAILED, and must be read from the body.

GEO_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.note: Geocoding is off the critical path — checkout against an ALREADY-SAVED address still works. Say that rather than blocking the sale.

BOT_GEO_CANDIDATE_EXPIRED.note: Re-run the search; never re-send coordinates the flow was holding.

DIGITAL_TOKEN_INVALID.note: Single-use and 15 minutes. Mint a fresh link.

BOT_SUPPORT_NO_CONTEXT.note: Fall through to platform support rather than saying nothing.

BOT_SUPPORT_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE.note: Most often /support:agency before an order has shipped. A legitimate empty answer.

copy_rules: Write in the customer's language, from customer.preferences.language, in one of en, fr, pt, es, ar.
Never show an error code, an HTTP status or a field path to a customer. requestId is the single exception, and only on internal and external_service.
Never say 'no account with that number', for any reason, on any path. It is a registration oracle and the platform is deliberately built not to be one.
Never explain WHY a product is unavailable. Draft, archived, suspended and deleted are one answer on purpose, so a competitor cannot enumerate a seller's unreleased catalogue.
Never turn a business_rule refusal into an apology. The rule is the answer; apologising for it implies it is a fault that might be waived.
Never promise a refund. Report the payment status the response carried — some gateways cannot refund at all and settle by hand.
Never claim a delivery outcome the platform did not state. estimatedDelivery is always null, and there are five customer-facing shipment words; anything else is invention.
